productBase.note: Tests only; no product, runtime or public API file is touched.

leadOrderedCorrections.correction: Its recoveryItemIds names REC-024 by mistake. Directive 0019 forbade starting REC-024; that record is the necessary turnout pre-block. REC-024 starts with directive 0021 on top of commit 17e6133b. The file stays byte-unchanged.
Its Quartz counters are stale after the added test identities. No old number is repeated as a current census; the census below is derived from the discovered case identities of the closing runs.

sixExplicitCases.timeControl: A shared test local control on the existing Quartz adjustment: AdvanceTime tracks the applied offset, ResetTime puts the clock back, and the fixture teardown restores the process wide provider even after a failure. No new product API.
sixExplicitCases.barriers: Every step waits for a message or scheduler barrier: the delivery counter of the schedule, the successful consume of the control command, and a horizon marker that lies between two due seconds.
removed: wall clock waits of ten and twenty seconds
large scheduler jumps that hope for a misfire

strengthened.cancel: delivers twice by construction, the cancel command is proven consumed, and the counter is unchanged after a horizon beyond the schedule
strengthened.pause: same construction for the pause command
strengthened.scheduleKey: ScheduleId and ScheduleGroup are compared against the identity of the schedule that produced the message, not against not null
strengthened.timeDomain: Scheduled, Sent, PreviousSent and NextScheduled must exist and be coherent: sent at or after scheduled, previous before sent, next after sent, and next exactly one interval after scheduled
strengthened.now: eight deliveries are reached by eight separate one second steps, each awaited, and the count stays eight beyond the end time
strengthened.futureCancel: the schedule is proven accepted, the cancel is proven consumed, the due time is passed under controlled time and the message is proven absent at a horizon marker

correctedOwnProbes.problem: run with a filter, where an Explicit case is not discovered at all and therefore never appears as not executed
correctedOwnProbes.fix: repeated unfiltered, where it is red

correctedOwnProbes.probe: missing time reset sabotage, first attempt
correctedOwnProbes.problem: only the SetUp reset was removed while the TearDown reset still put the clock back, so the probe was not discriminating
correctedOwnProbes.fix: repeated without any reset, where it is red

residualRaceFoundAndFixed: The first version of the cancel and pause cases read a counter after a horizon marker. With a concurrent endpoint the marker handler can finish before an earlier interval handler, and the unfiltered project run showed the resulting off by one. The baseline is now built by awaiting a known number of deliveries, the horizon lies between two due seconds, and the endpoint processes one message at a time.

turnoutAssertions.replaced: await InMemoryTestHarness.Consumed.Any<ScheduleMessage>() in the two accepted turnout fixtures is now an assertion bound to the test cancellation token
turnoutAssertions.flakyKept: Ten fixtures of the Quartz project keep the category. It is no execution filter: the closing run is unfiltered and green.

cronCases.confirmedCause: The test converted 1 October once from local time to UTC and reused that UTC hour for every day. On 31 October 2010 the local zone leaves daylight saving time, so the same UTC hour is a different local cron time. This is a test data defect, not a product defect.
cronCases.fix: Every checked calendar day builds its own local cron time and converts it, exactly as the sibling cases in the same file already do. No product change.
cronCases.negative: The same run against the previous test file under TZ=Europe/Berlin fails with expected day of 31 for both cases
cronCases.note: Under the canonical runner the timezone is pinned to UTC, where no transition exists and both cases were green even unfixed. The defect only shows in a zone with daylight saving time.

openAgainstTheDirective.reason: Those are the inherited Explicit cases of the core project, benchmarks, manual observation cases and timing sensitive cases. They are listed in the not-executed inventory, which is why the category gate passes.
openAgainstTheDirective.disposition: Reworking them is a scope expansion beyond this block and belongs to the separate obligation of REQ-CLEAN-005 for benchmarks and human diagnosis cases. Reported, not silently accepted, and not repaired here.
